title: Mathlib Imports
content: Imports six Mathlib modules: InnerProductSpace.Basic for EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2), MetricSpace.Basic for the dist function, Finset.Basic and Finset.Card for finite point sets and offDiag enumeration, Filter.Basic for the atTop filter used in asymptotic statements, and Tactic for general automation.
mathContext: The formalization uses `EuclideanSpace \mathbb{R} (\text{Fin}\,2)` as the type of points in $\mathbb{R}^2$, which carries both the inner product structure and the induced metric `dist`.

title: Unit Distance Pairs Count
content: Counts unordered pairs of distinct points at Euclidean distance exactly 1. Uses offDiag filtering on Finset of points in ℝ², divided by 2 for unordered pairs.
mathContext: For a finite set $S \subset \mathbb{R}^2$, defines $\text{udpc}(S) = |\{(p, q) \in S \times S : p \neq q,\, \|p - q\| = 1\}| / 2$. The `offDiag` function produces all ordered pairs $(p, q)$ with $p \neq q$; dividing by 2 converts to unordered pairs $\{p, q\}$.

title: Achievable Unit Distance Counts
content: The set unitDistanceCounts(n) collects all possible values of unitDistancePairsCount over n-point configurations. This is the set whose supremum defines u(n).
mathContext: Defines $\mathcal{U}(n) = \{\text{udpc}(S) : S \subset \mathbb{R}^2,\, |S| = n\}$, the range of the unit distance counting function over all $n$-point configurations. This is a subset of $\mathbb{N}$ whose supremum is the extremal function $u(n)$.

title: Maximum Unit Distances u(n)
content: The function u(n) = max over all n-point configurations of the number of unit-distance pairs. Defined as sSup of the set of achievable counts.
mathContext: Defines $u(n) = \sup \mathcal{U}(n) = \sup\{\text{udpc}(S) : |S| = n\}$. The use of `sSup` (supremum in a conditionally complete lattice) requires the set to be bounded above, which is axiomatized in `unitDistanceCounts_bddAbove`.

title: Well-Definedness of u(n)
content: The set of achievable unit distance counts is bounded above, ensuring that sSup (and hence u(n)) is well-defined. The bound is C(n,2) = n(n-1)/2, the total number of unordered pairs.
mathContext: Axiomatizes $\mathcal{U}(n) \subseteq [0, \binom{n}{2}]$: since there are at most $\binom{n}{2}$ unordered pairs, the set of achievable unit distance counts is bounded. This ensures $u(n) = \mathrm{sSup}(\mathcal{U}(n))$ is a natural number rather than $\infty$.

title: Spencer–Szemerédi–Trotter Bound
content: u(n) = O(n^{4/3}), proved in 1984 using the Szemerédi–Trotter incidence theorem. This is the best known upper bound and has stood for over 40 years.
mathContext: States $\exists C > 0,\, \forall n \geq 1: u(n) \leq C \cdot n^{4/3}$. The proof reduces unit distances to point-circle incidences: for each point $p_i$, the unit circle $C_i = \{q : |p_i - q| = 1\}$ contributes incidences with other points. The Szemerédi–Trotter theorem bounds $I(P, \mathcal{C}) = O(|P|^{2/3} |\mathcal{C}|^{2/3} + |P| + |\mathcal{C}|)$, giving $O(n^{4/3})$ when $|P| = |\mathcal{C}| = n$.

title: Lattice Lower Bound
content: Integer lattice constructions achieve n^{1+c/log log n} unit distances, establishing the conjectured order of magnitude from below.
mathContext: States $\exists c > 0$ such that $\forall^\infty n: u(n) \geq n^{1+c/\log\log n}$. The construction uses $\sqrt{n} \times \sqrt{n}$ integer lattice points and exploits the fact that the number of representations of an integer $m$ as $m = a^2 + b^2$ is $r_2(m) = 4 \sum_{d|m} \chi(d)$ where $\chi$ is the non-principal character mod 4. Choosing $m$ with many small prime factors $\equiv 1 \pmod{4}$ maximizes $r_2(m)$, yielding the $n^{c/\log\log n}$ factor.

title: OpenAI 2026 Construction (Reported Disproof of Erdős's Exponent)
content: On 2026-05-20 OpenAI announced an AI-assisted construction reportedly disproving the conjectured exponent in u(n). The construction replaces the Gaussian integer lattice with rings of integers in number fields admitting infinite class field towers, whose unit groups generate substantially more unit-length differences than ℤ². Peer review is pending; the Spencer–Szemerédi–Trotter O(n^{4/3}) upper bound is unaffected.
mathContext:
Erdős (1946) conjectured $u(n) = n^{1+O(1/\log\log n)}$, i.e. the $\sqrt{n} \times \sqrt{n}$ integer lattice (achieving $n \cdot \exp(c \log n / \log\log n)$) is essentially optimal. OpenAI's construction (announced 2026-05-20) reportedly produces an infinite family of point sets in $\mathbb{R}^2$ yielding a **polynomial improvement** over Erdős's lower bound. The mechanism: pick an algebraic number field $K$ whose ring of integers $\mathcal{O}_K$ admits an **infinite class field tower**, guaranteed to exist by the **Golod–Shafarevich theorem** when the $\ell$-rank of the class group of $K$ is sufficiently large relative to $\sqrt{[K : \mathbb{Q}]}$. The unit group $\mathcal{O}_K^\times$ then provides exponentially many algebraic relations of norm 1, which (after embedding $\mathcal{O}_K$ into $\mathbb{C} \cong \mathbb{R}^2$) translate to many unit-length differences.

**Status (peer review pending).** This disproves the conjectured upper bound on the *exponent* of $u(n)$; it does not disprove the SST $O(n^{4/3})$ upper bound, which is unaffected. The true asymptotic order of $u(n)$ remains an open problem. Until the OpenAI write-up is peer-reviewed and erdosproblems.com#90 is reclassified, this gallery entry retains `status: axiomatized`, `badge: wip`, and `erdosProblemStatus: open`.

title: Point-Set Extraction Map + Counting Scaffold (OpenAI2026LowerBound.lean)
content: The companion file Proofs/Erdos90/OpenAI2026LowerBound.lean formalizes the combinatorial/geometric core of the OpenAI 2026 construction. It defines a concrete point-set extraction map pointSet K φ₀ φ₁ r : Finset (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)) — the finite lattice points of 𝓞_K inside a ball (via Mathlib's NumberField.canonicalEmbedding.integerLattice.inter_ball_finite) projected to the plane by the real parts at two chosen complex embeddings. The counting lemma (many unit-distance pairs from the algebraic structure) is stated as two axioms pending the peer-reviewed OpenAI formula, and the headline lower bound openai_2026_unit_distance_lower_bound is left as sorry until the published exponent α is fixed.
mathContext: The extraction map is the honest planar shadow of the algebraic point set: for a number field $K$ of a high tower level, the canonical (Minkowski) embedding $\iota : K \hookrightarrow (K \to_{+*} \mathbb{C}) \to \mathbb{C}$ restricts on $\mathcal{O}_K$ to a lattice whose intersection with a ball of radius $r$ is **finite** (Mathlib: `integerLattice.inter_ball_finite`). Reading off two coordinates (real parts at chosen embeddings $\varphi_0, \varphi_1$) lands the configuration in $\mathbb{R}^2 = $ `EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)`, exactly the type consumed by `unitDistancePairsCount`. This part is fully constructive (0 axioms; `pointSet_card_le` bounds its cardinality). The **counting bound** $\#\{\text{unit-distance pairs}\} \ge m^{1+\alpha_0}$ and the **transfer** to $u(n) = $ `maxUnitDistances n` are axiomatized (`unitDistanceCountingBound`, `towerYieldsGrowingPointSets`) because the explicit exponent and unit-count formula await the peer-reviewed OpenAI publication (parent tracker #20576's external blocker). The reduction wires three dependencies: (i) class field tower existence (`ClassFieldTower.lean`), (ii) Golod–Shafarevich infinitude (`GolodShafarevich.lean`), (iii) the local counting lemma. The `PointSetExtraction` structure bundles the construction output ($\alpha > 0$ with the eventual bound) so that `lowerBound_of_extraction` discharges the headline once a concrete peer-reviewed instantiation is supplied.
